newsitem.title: USA: AtHome sees service in all top U.S., Canada cities.
newsitem.headline: AtHome sees service in all top U.S., Canada cities.

text.p: AtHome Network Senior Vice President Dean Gilbert said on Wednesday a deal with two Canadian cable companies will help it roll out service in 25 to 30 large North American cities by the end of 1997.

"We're in a very dramatic growth phase," said Gilbert. He said the deal with the Canadian companies should help AtHome build a presence for its Internet services "in every major city in both countries by the end of this year."
The company already has begun commercial deployments in a number of communities across the United States, Gilbert said.
AtHome distributes high-speed interactive services to homes and businesses using hybrid-fiber coaxial links and its own Internet backbone, or core network.

AtHome Network has developed an infrastructure which can store and replicate data from the Internet for delivery in a high-performance "parallel" Internet network, bringing the data closer to the customer for improved accesss.
The aim is to reduce traffic jams and bottlenecks that are becoming common on the Internet and provide reliable high-speed service.

With the Canadian firms, Rogers Communications Inc. and Shaw Communications Inc., AtHome said it will create WAVE@Home, a service that will extend high-speed Internet access over cable networks in Canada through a broadband Internet backbone.

The service will be co-branded and will be able to reach approximately five million households in Canada, or about 50 percent of the country's market, with more than two million of those becoming "WAVE-ready" homes by the end of 1997.

Gilbert said around 40 million homes in the United States are bypassed by cable systems which could eventually carry AtHome services under current partnerships. With the Canada deal, it could now reach nearly half of North American homes.
But he declined to say how quickly AtHome expects its subscriber base to grow or how many homes will be reached by its Internet access systems by the end of 1997.
"We're in a competitive environment," he said. "It is not our desire to tell the world."
The two Canadian companies will be making an unspecified minority investment in AtHome, and will seek to bring further Canadian cable suppliers into the WAVE group.

AtHome was formed in 1995 with financing from cable operators and the venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers. Investors include Tele-Communications Inc., Comcast Corp and Cox Communications.

AtHome incorporates the "@" symbol, common in electronic mail addresses, as the first character of its name. In this story, the word "At" is used to represent the encircled "a" symbol for publishing services which do not support it.
